turns.text:
Two years ago my ex and I agreed in writing that our son gets a smartphone at 13. His exact words were "Agreed. 13." On Saturday, at Felix's 11th birthday party, in front of nine of his friends, Hector handed him a wrapped smartphone. He didn't tell me he was buying it. I found out when Felix unwrapped it. What was I supposed to do, pull it out of his hands at his own party? I told Hector quietly that we'd agreed on 13. He said we'd talk this week. He hasn't called.

In August he asked about revisiting it for the bus, "even a basic one," and I asked to talk once school started. That was the last I heard of a basic phone. He went around me, bought a full smartphone, and sprang it on me at his party.

So at my house it went in my desk. Felix told me his dad was just being nice. On Wednesday I sent it with him to his dad's and told Hector it doesn't come back to my house. I think he wanted to be the hero of the party. I feel steamrolled, and I'm angry.

How do I get him to see that what we agree on has to mean something?

You feel steamrolled, and you're angry. You had his "Agreed. 13." in writing, you found out about the phone at the same moment as Felix and nine of his friends, and you were left choosing between letting it go and taking a gift out of your son's hands at his own party. Then "we'll talk this week" was followed by silence. That sounds hard and lonely, and it makes sense that the silence is adding to the anger.

I've only heard your side, so I can't tell you who's in the wrong. Hector would likely tell this differently, and I don't know how. "He wanted to be the hero" is your read of why he did it. He might describe it another way, and I'd hold that guess loosely until you've heard from him.

**What each of you would probably need to show**

- **For you:** that "13" was meant to hold unless you both agreed to change it, and that a request in August followed by "let's talk once school starts" wasn't agreement.
- **For Hector:** how he understood things after August. Did he think the conversation was still open, already settled, or stalled? Why a full smartphone instead of the "basic one" he'd mentioned? Why didn't he tell you first?

**Questions worth asking him**

- When he bought it, how was he thinking about the written agreement?
- Did he see your August reply as a no, a delay, or something else?
- When he says "we'll talk," what does he want that talk to settle?

**One possible step**

You could send a message about how the two of you change decisions, rather than about the phone itself. For example:

*"You said we'd talk this week, and I'd still like to. I'm less focused on the phone right now than on how we change things we've agreed on. Can we set a time? I want to hear how you were thinking about it, and I'd like us to agree that changes to things we've put in writing get talked through first, before either of us acts."*

This puts your main point (that agreements have to mean something) on the table. It also invites his account before either of you argues the phone itself. Whether to send it, and whether it fits how the two of you talk, is your call.

You're right to feel what you feel. Finding out at the same moment as Felix, in front of his friends, after a written "Agreed. 13," and then hearing nothing after "we'll talk this week": feeling steamrolled and angry about that makes sense, and I'm not questioning it.

Whether you're right about the disagreement itself, I can't tell you, and it wouldn't be fair to you if I pretended I could. I've only heard your side. What's still open is how Hector understood things after August, why he went ahead without telling you, and what he'd say about the agreement now. His answers might make things look the way you see them, or they might add something neither of us knows yet.

If I just said "yes, you're right," it might feel good for a minute, but it wouldn't help with what you actually asked: getting him to see that your agreements mean something. That's more likely to come from hearing his account and then agreeing together on how changes get made. The message I suggested is one way in, if you want it.
